unresolvedReferences.description: The Mount Tai sacrifice is dated by inference to 725, which makes Liu Yan born c. 718.
His Xia magistracy is dated only to the Tianbao era (742–756).
The dismissal of Zheng Shuqing and Li Qiwu and Yan Zhuang's accusation are inferred as c. 761.
The letter to Yuan Zai is inferred as c. 764.
The shared control of finances with Di Wuqi is inferred as c. 766.
Duke Huan and Duke Wen are Spring and Autumn allusions (BCE, which the schema cannot date) and were disposed as titles; chief minister Xiao Hua was not offered as a candidate and was not extracted.
Death at 65 in 780 implies birth c. 716; chunk 001's age 8 at the Mount Tai sacrifice (725) implies c. 718.
The Consort Dugu intrigue is inferred as c. 775; the Prince of Han was not offered as a person candidate.
The finance officials' tenure is inferred as c. 785; Chen Jian's treatise c. 800; Han Huang's demotion of Yuan Xiu c. 786.
Guan Zhong and Xiao He are pre-Tang allusions (BCE, which the schema cannot date) and were disposed as unresolved.
The Jiang-Huai rebels are dated only to the Shangyuan–Baoying period (760–762).
The Four Scholars of Wu (Bao Rong, He Zhizhang, Zhang Xu, Zhang Ruoxu) are dated c. 720 by inference.
Lu Zheng's appointment to Tong Prefecture during Dou Can's ascendancy is inferred as c. 790.
Li Ruochu's career and Li Peng are inferred c. 785; succession to Wang Wei c. 796.
Liu Zongjing's later career is undated (c. 800 inferred).
Shi Hui's death at the hands of mutineers is undated (c. 765 inferred).
Du Cong's tenure at the Bureau of Revenue is inferred c. 845.
The Shannan bandit episode (Cui Xuan, Feng Ao) is inferred c. 850.
Li Fu's Nanzhao campaign and Liu Tong's Xichuan posting are inferred c. 866–867; Liu Tong's death is undated.
Two different emperors are rendered 'Emperor Xuanzong' in English (宣宗 at s0184, 玄宗 at s0207); kept as separate people.
Units s0226–s0236 continue Di Wuqi's biography with no explicit name in this chunk, so his later career (Lang Prefecture, Duke of Fufeng, death at 71 c. 780) has no surface to attach to here.
Di Wuqi's son Feng and daughter-in-law Lady Zheng are undated (c. 780 inferred).
Ban Jingqian is dated c. 730 by inference.
Li Baochen died in 781 (inferred from external context); the evaluation dispute with Cui Ning and Liu Nai is inferred to the same period.
李希烈 (Li Xilie) is rendered 'Li Xiyan' in the translation; linked to the zh name.
衛尉卿 is the Court of the Imperial Guard, not the Imperial Stud as translated.
Zhang Pang/Ban Hong dispute dated c. 790–792 by inference; Wang Duan and friends c. 750; Wang Shao's death (age 72) undated, c. 814 inferred; An Jinda and Tang Chongjing c. 807.
Dou Can's demotion to Chen Prefecture and execution dated 792–793 by inference; Cheng Yi's recommendation c. 806.
